items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to a license to sell liquor at retail for consumption on certain premises
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1030

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law,
in relation to a license to sell liquor at retail for consumption on
certain premises

 PURPOSE :

This bill would allow Tony & Nick's Italian Kitchen to obtain a full
liquor license for the on-premises consumption of alcohol.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1: Amends subdivision 7 of section 64 of the Alcohol Beverage
Control Law, adding a new paragraph (e-8) to allow the issuance of a
retail license for on-premises consumption of alcohol for a premises
within 200 feet of a school or place of worship, provided that the
purpose of such premises is for the sale and consumption of food or
beverage, and such premises is within the boundaries of Ulster County
as directed therein.

Section 2: Effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Tony & Nick's Italian Kitchen is a casual Italian dining and catering
establishment in the Village of Ellenville, New York with a currently
valid beer and wine license. While the Alcoholic Beverage Control Law
prohibits the sale for on-premises consumption of alcohol at any
location within 200 feet of a place of worship or school, exceptions
have been made for certain establishments that do not pose problems
for the place of worship, school, or surrounding neighborhood.

Tony & Nick's is located in a restaurant cluster that serves as a
catalyst for renewed economic growth in the Village of Ellenville,
which is nestled in the foothills of the Shawangunk Mountains ranges
in Southwestern Ulster County. By providing Tony & Nick's with an
exemption to the current provision, it will be in a position to draw
in tourists by not only offering a fine dining menu but also by
meeting customer expectations with an inventory of local and
international alcoholic beverages. Additionally, a separate
restaurant, Aroma Thyme Bistro, which is located directly across the
street from Tony & Nicks, received a similar exemption in 2005.
Further, the church that is located within 200 feet of the restaurant
utilizes a main entrance that is separate and farther away from the
entrance stated by the property's official address.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

S.7653 of 2016: Passed Senate, Died in Assembly Economic Development

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
